title: Jujutsu Kaisen
subtitle: The strength that doesn't need an audience
_guide_hero: Layout: Title (1-4 words), jpTitle (1-3 words), subtitle (3-6 words). Poster is right split image (2:3 portrait).

entry._guide: Layout: Centered giant text. Limit 15-40 words.
entry.breathQuote: I came for the fights and stayed for the wage. It was the first action show where the strongest character I knew had a job, a schedule, and a quiet hatred of overtime.

reflection._guide: Layout: Right column split. Quote: 20-50 words. Tags: 2-4 items. Cards: 30-70 words.
reflection.quote: It kept telling me everyone is going to die — and then it kept making me care anyway. That's when I understood what it was really about: choosing purpose despite the expiration date.
reflection.whatIKept: You can carry something heavy without needing anyone to know it's heavy. Nanami never made his burden visible — he just carried it, every day, until he couldn't.
reflection.definingScene: Nanami walking into Shibuya knowing he won't walk out. No rage. No monologue. Just a man finishing what he accepted long ago.
reflection.whoItMadeMeThinkAbout: My father, the morning he drove three hours in silence to help me move apartments, and drove back without once asking for thanks.

thoughtCascade.thought: The animation is stunning. I told myself this was just spectacle.
Wait — he's not fighting to win. He's fighting because it's his job.
That scene with Nanami stayed in my head for three days.
I paused. I rewound. I watched it again without sound.
I understood something about my father I didn't have words for before.

_guide_thoughtCascade: Layout: Left-aligned timeline. Thought: 20-45 words. Micro: 2-5 words.

cinematicMoment._guide: Layout: Full width dark section. Body: 40-80 words. Image: 16:9 landscape.
cinematicMoment.title: He walked in knowing he wouldn't walk out.
cinematicMoment.body: No music swell. No slow-motion last breath. Just a man with a clear understanding of what the job required, and a quiet decision to do it completely.

memoryCards._guide: Layout: Hovering glass cards. Question: 5-12 words. Cards: text 30-50 words.
memoryCards.question: What stayed with me after the screen went dark?

cards.title: The Overtime
cards.text: Nanami clocks out of his office job and into a worse one. Showing up for work that's yours is the whole discipline.

cards.title: The Finger
cards.text: Yuji swallows it to save someone else's life. He didn't choose his inheritance — he chose what direction to carry it.

cards.title: The Expiration Date
cards.text: Everyone dies anyway. The show never lets you forget it — and it never lets you use it as an excuse.

altMemories.question: What quietly changed?
altMemories.heading: My definition of strength got smaller and more precise.
altMemories.body: Strength used to mean capability. Now it means execution without drama — doing the thing without needing the thing to feel meaningful in the moment.
altMemories.caption: Strength without an audience.

altMemories.question: What caught my attention?
altMemories.heading: The fight choreography is a distraction. Deliberately.
altMemories.body: The action exists to pull you past your guard. Before you realize it, you're attached to people the story is about to take from you. That's not style — that's architecture.
altMemories.caption: The real trap is caring.

_guide_altMemories: Layout: Alternating split layout. Body: 50-100 words. Image: 1:1 or 4:5.

pullQuote._guide: Layout: Giant dramatic quote. Text: 10-30 words.
pullQuote.text: You're strong. That's your flaw. You're too strong, so you've forgotten what it means to be weak.

timeline._guide: Layout: Center timeline nodes. Body: 30-60 words.

firstImpression.heading: The animation pulled me in first
firstImpression.body: Fast, fluid, technically stunning. I thought I was watching a sport — spectacular choreography. For a while, that was enough.

whatShifted.heading: Then Nanami walked onscreen
whatShifted.body: Someone who had seen through the fantasy of heroism and continued anyway. Not for glory — because the alternative was letting someone else bear it.

whatStayed.heading: Strength without sentiment
whatStayed.body: Not every hard thing deserves a narrative arc. Some things you do quietly, completely, without asking the universe to acknowledge the difficulty.

items.line: when I'm adding drama to something that doesn't need it.
whether my idea of strength requires an audience.
to finish what I start without needing it to feel heroic.
the word 'sacrifice' for what was just ordinary responsibility.

characters.name: Nanami Kento
characters.mirror: He showed me professionalism divorced from ego. He hates the system he works in and continues anyway, because someone has to. I think about that every time I'm tempted to make my frustration visible.

characters.name: Itadori Yuji
characters.mirror: What do you do with a terrible inheritance? He didn't choose his situation. He chose what direction to carry it.

characters.name: Gojo Satoru
characters.mirror: Confidence so complete it doesn't require validation is disarming. Not arrogance — certainty. I spent a long time thinking they were the same thing.

notes.text: The show keeps reminding you that everyone is going to die. And then it keeps making you care anyway. That's the whole point.
I don't think Nanami wanted to be remembered. I think he just wanted to have done it right.

ideas.application: Negative things accumulate invisibly and become destructive when not released. I started scheduling deliberate decompression after this.
Forcing your environment to match your internal state. Total focus is a weapon — and most people never deploy it.

continueJourney.because: Because I still ask myself — before I complain about a long day — whether I'm doing the work for the work's sake or for the audience.
